Cloying

KLOY-ing · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Cloying is disgustingly sweet or so excessively emotional that it becomes unpleasant.

The birthday card's cloying rhymes made her groan rather than smile.

Worked Example

The frosting was so cloying that even the children could only manage a few bites.

The sweetness wasn't just strong -- it was so overwhelming that it became unpleasant, which is exactly cloying.

How Cloying Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

gushing

gushing: excessively sweet or emotional, especially in a false way

sickly

sickly: unpleasantly excessive, especially in sweetness

Antonyms

tart

tart: sharp or sour in taste, or blunt in tone

How Strong Is It? — sweet → cloying → nauseating

sweet vs. cloying

sweet vs. cloying: Something sweet is simply pleasant; something cloying is so overwhelmingly sweet that it becomes unpleasant.

nauseating vs. cloying

nauseating vs. cloying: Cloying describes an unpleasant excess of sweetness or emotion; nauseating is stronger still, causing actual physical discomfort.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Cloying comes from the older verb cloy, itself shortened from Middle English acloien, 'to hinder or clog,' ultimately related to Latin clavus, 'a nail.'

Use the root in a new word: clog

Use the root in a new word: clog: The same acloien root is distantly related to the everyday word clog, both carrying the idea of something becoming blocked or overloaded.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Cloying can describe literal taste (an overly sweet dessert) or a non-literal tone (overly emotional writing, music, or speech).
